newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate falls sharply on heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate falls sharply on heavy demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates fell 160 basis points to close at 21.40 percent due to heavy demand by big players with large liquidity positions, analysts and traders said.
"Overnight rates fell again because dealers who were very liquid decided to step in and buy and it is very likely we will see primary rates fall tomorrow," a money market analyst said.
The analyst added that rates also fell in response to Banco de Mexico's recent decision to raise limits on the outstanding balances it would allow commercial banks to have.
"That made overnight rates cheaper and eased upside pressure and those who were liquid felt the market was running away from them," he said.
Dealers said a favorable outlook for forthcoming inflation data and forecast cuts in primary interest rates at Tuesday evening's central bank auction also helped secondary rates to slide.
"All we are waiting for now is inflation, on Thursday, and we expect the figures to be positive," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico is expected to release inflation data for April 1-15 on Thursday.
Mexico City financial houses surveyed by Reuters MXAAP, forecast an average rise of 0.64 percent in consumer prices for the first half of April.
Banco de Mexico drained liquidity of 7.483 billion pesos from the system through a combination of three direct sales of Cetes and nine repurchase agreements.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, fell 100 basis points to close at 22.00 percent.
June contracts on Cetes futures traded on the Chicago mercantile exchange closed down 10 centavos at 78.15 pesos.
Liquidity of 7.283 billion pesos was programmed to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
